property_summary: For any caller and any inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increments proposalCount by 1 (i.e., proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant omits the increment so for some inputs the post-call proposalCount does not increase and thus violates this rule.

For any caller and any inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increases proposalCount by exactly 1; the mutant that removes the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that removes the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged, so there exist inputs where that equality fails.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) increments proposalCount (proposalCount_after > proposalCount_before); the mutant that omits the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged, so there exist inputs where this property is violated.

For any caller and inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increases proposalCount by 1 (proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that removed the increment can leave proposalCount unchanged, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any recipient/amount, calling newGrantProposal increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (reference); the mutant sometimes increases it by 2 due to an extra increment, so proposalCount after the call differs from expected by one for some inputs.

For any inputs, calling newGrantProposal(...) on the correct contract increments (or at least does not reset) proposalCount away from 0 so that proposalCount != 0 after the call (i.e., it does not force proposalCount to a constant 1); the mutant resets proposalCount to 1, causing proposalCount to be equal to 1 regardless of prior value and thus differing from the reference for some inputs.

For any caller and any (recipient, amount), calling newGrantProposal increases proposalCount from its previous value (i.e., proposalCount after the call is strictly greater than the prior proposalCount); the mutant that resets proposalCount to 1 violates this when prior proposalCount != 0 and not equal to 1.

For any prior proposalCount and any newGrantProposal inputs, calling newGrantProposal never decreases proposalCount (i.e., proposalCount_after >= proposalCount_before); the mutant that assigns proposalCount = 1 can decrease it for some prior values, violating this invariant.

For any starting proposalCount and any caller/parameters, after calling newGrantProposal(...) the contract's proposalCount is not equal to 1 if the previous proposalCount was not 1 (i.e., newGrantProposal does not forcibly reset proposalCount to a constant 1); the mutant that assigns proposalCount = 1 violates this for inputs where prior proposalCount != 1.

For any initial proposalCount and any inputs to newGrantProposal, calling newGrantProposal increases proposalCount by exactly 1 (i.e., proposalCount_after == proposalCount_before + 1); the mutant that sets proposalCount = 1 breaks this when proposalCount_before != 0 or != 0/other values.
After init(...), the recorded VADER address equals the first input parameter _vader.
After init, the VADER address differs from the USDV address (VADER != USDV).
After initializing the contract via init, the VADER and USDV addresses must be different (VADER != USDV).
After init, the VADER address stored in c is not equal to the VAULT address (VADER != VAULT).
After initializing C with given addresses, the stored VADER and stored VAULT addresses must differ (VADER != VAULT).
After init(...), the public VADER getter equals the _vader argument passed to init

After init(...) and newAddressProposal(...), calling finaliseProposal on a UTILS-type proposal succeeds (does not revert) because VADER was set in init in P but is zero in M, causing a revert when moveUtils(...) is executed.
After init, the VADER address stored in the contract must equal the first init argument (non-zero if caller provides non-zero).
After init, the USDV getter returns the second init parameter (_usdv), not the first (_vader).
After init, the stored USDV address is different from VAULT (i.e., USDV != VAULT).
After initializing C via init(...), the stored USDV and VAULT addresses must be different (USDV != VAULT).
